review: nani-cull-a vs nani-cull-b (independent reconstructions of the nani GPU cull/draw-list chain + wall family)
method: Per-file comparison of candidate A/B HLSL against the ground-truth .bin. Ground truth read from /Users/yuluo/Desktop/game/ljxsj_92385/Tiny Glade/compiled-shaders/. Modules extracted at SPIR-V magic offset 23/24 and disassembled with tools/render-passes/dump_spv_ops.py (word-level). Every candidate HLSL was recompiled with the SAME dxc 1.10.2605.37 and structurally compared via tools/render-passes/recompile_check.py; for the no-hzb variant bins I compiled B manually with `-D TINYGLADE_NANI_NO_HZB` (recompile_check has no -D passthrough) and compared the fingerprint with tools/render-passes/spirv_parse.py. Embedded OpSource/OpString include-closure lists (validation/compile-commands.json embedded_source_paths) and embedded OpMemberName struct tables (skeleton/raw-per-bin.jsonl) were used as additional structural oracles beyond the original hard gate. Documented dxc-version residuals (OpBitcast-in-RWByteAddressBuffer, OpLine/OpSource/OpString closure counts, OpExtInstImport, ternary->OpSwitch) are NOT preference grounds.

hard_gate.summary: Both sides PASS bindings/entry/LocalSize/capabilities on every non-physical nani compute module and the wall compute modules (independently re-verified). B additionally passes the 10 PhysicalStorageBufferAddresses cull bins (base/curved_halftimber/plaster/smoke/stairs_floor, both hzb 8a7d2f81 and no-hzb d8520a92) by declaring `[[vk::ext_capability(5347)]]` with a uint2 address (no Int64) and approximating the instance read; A's cull_and_bucket.cs uses `[[vk::buffer_reference]]`/uint64_t and does not compile with the installed dxc (FAIL_DXC). B is the only side that reproduces the no-hzb binding set (verified by manual -D compile: exact 10-binding set, no hzb_tex/\$Globals, caps Shader+RuntimeDescriptorArray+PhysicalStorageBufferAddresses). B has 4 full structural PASS (clear_histogram, clear_subtotals, draw_indexed_indirect_to_dispatch, fill_unsorted_instance_indirection); A has 0. A is missing 8 cull-family variants, the wall rasters, and nani/inc/user.hlsl outright.

pba.winner: B strategy (uint2 + ext_capability 5347); A's uint64/buffer_reference is the wrong structure even if it compiled
pba.bin_opcode_evidence: Disassembly of _nani_cull_and_bucket.cs.hlsl_cs_main_8a7d2f81e72c8eeb.bin: capability list is exactly {Shader 1, RuntimeDescriptorArray 5302, PhysicalStorageBufferAddresses 5347} - NO Int64 (5349). OpMemoryModel 5348 (PhysicalStorageBuffer64). Only OpTypeInt 32-bit exist (no 64-bit integer type). Push constant member 0 is loaded as `OpLoad uint2`; the offset is added with a 32-bit `OpIAdd` on the LOW word only (no carry propagation into the high word); the uint2 address is then converted to a pointer with `OpBitcast <ptr PhysicalStorageBuffer> <- uint2`, and the instance record is read with `OpLoad uint4 <ptr> alignment 2 volatile` directly from the PhysicalStorageBuffer pointer (no OpAccessChain on the physical pointer). A's own header comment ('manual uint2 carry add, no Int64 capability') correctly identifies this, but A's source actually uses uint64_t + buffer_reference, which dxc would compile to Int64 + 64-bit IAdd - mismatching the bin. B's decisions.md claim ('the original kept the address as uint2 and had no Int64') is confirmed verbatim.
pba.adjudication: B is closer to the bin's actual opcode structure (uint2 address, no Int64, 5347 capability) AND is the better reconstruction strategy (compiles, passes the hard gate, keeps the uint2 representation). Residual: neither side reproduces the genuine OpBitcast-to-PhysicalStorageBuffer + volatile OpLoad physical read; B substitutes a logical per-index read and A does not compile. The faithful physical load (uint2 -> OpBitcast ptr -> OpLoad) is not expressible with the installed dxc, so B's approximation + a documented residual note is the practical ceiling. A's file is a useful algorithm reference for that residual.

hzB_variant.evidence: The 8a7d2f81/d8520a92 pair differs ONLY by the hzb_tex (t21) + $Globals (b22) bindings and the 2x2 mip test; B's default compilation matches 8a7d (bindings t13..t22 incl hzb_tex/$Globals), and a manual -D TINYGLADE_NANI_NO_HZB compile matches d852 exactly (t13..t20, no hzb_tex/$Globals). The bin's hzb test is 4 x OpImageFetch at (coord, coord+1, mip) 2x2 + min, consistent with B's approximated 2x2 sample. W22 (first round) runs the no-hzb variant, W28 (second round, after generate_hzb) runs the hzb variant.

wall/generate_draw_lists.cs.hlsl.evidence: Both hard-gate PASS on cs_pass1/cs_pass2. Bin disasm of cs_pass1 shows: 4-plane frustum loop (OpDot) then the visibility branch - `if (prev_visibility & bit) { InterlockedOr(next_visibility, bit); LOD-bucket append }`, and the screen-space LOD ring-bucket loop (buckets 4..7, AtomicIAdd on draw_commands instance_count + brick_draw_list store) runs UNCONDITIONALLY after the frustum test (ring code is reached from both branches; no early-return). A's cs_pass1 has the frustum test + LOD + ring buckets (closer to bin structure, 82-key residual) BUT gates everything behind `if (!was_visible) return;` - wrong (bin runs ring appends for non-prev-visible bricks). B's cs_pass1 omits the frustum test and the ring buckets entirely (89-key residual) and does InterlockedOr unconditionally - farther from bin structure. cs_pass2 bin has 4 OpImageFetch (2x2 HZB) + 13 matrix ops (8-corner AABB screen bounds) - A's cs_pass2 approximates this; B's is a 2x2 sample. Merge: B's binding shell (RWStructuredBuffer draw_commands u13, frame_constants_storage_buffer t1/s1, $Globals b14) + A's body, with the bin's exact gating (LOD append + InterlockedOr only when prev-visible AND in-frustum; ring append unconditional).
